name: Rapids Bite Kitchen
description: A fast-casual restaurant in Grand Rapids' Wealthy Street corridor, known for globally-inspired grain bowls, wraps, and fresh-pressed juices. Opened in 2019 by couple Ethan and Priya Okafor, survived COVID by pivoting to delivery and takeout. Now doing $1.4M annually across dine-in, takeout, delivery (DoorDash, Uber Eats), and catering. Built a loyal local following but operations are chaotic and margins are thin.

team.name: Ethan Okafor
team.responsibilities: Menu development, kitchen management, food ordering. Works 60+ hours/week. Does all ingredient ordering from memory and gut instinct.

team.name: Priya Okafor
team.responsibilities: Front of house, marketing, social media, catering sales, HR. Also works 60+ hours/week. Managing everything that isn't the kitchen.

team.name: Dante Williams
team.responsibilities: Runs the kitchen when Ethan isn't there. Manages 6 line cooks. Handles food prep scheduling.

team.name: Line Cooks
team.responsibilities: Mix of full-time and part-time. High turnover — 3 left in the last 6 months.

team.name: Front of House Staff
team.responsibilities: Cashiers, counter service, delivery prep. Also high turnover.

team.name: Nadia Hassan
team.responsibilities: Handles catering inquiries and orders. Part-time. Uses a paper notebook to track everything.

team.name: External Bookkeeper
team.responsibilities: Comes in biweekly. Uses QuickBooks. Always behind on reconciliation.

toolStack.name: Toast POS
toolStack.usage: Point of sale and payment processing. Generates sales reports that Priya reviews weekly — when she remembers.
painPoints: Sales data not connected to inventory or ordering decisions
Reports reviewed weekly at best — no real-time visibility
No automated alerts for slow-moving items or top sellers

toolStack.name: DoorDash Tablet
toolStack.usage: Third-party delivery orders. Separate physical tablet for DoorDash.
painPoints: Separate tablet from Uber Eats — staff must monitor two screens
Menu updates must be done manually on each platform separately
No integration with Toast POS for unified order tracking

toolStack.name: Uber Eats Tablet
toolStack.usage: Third-party delivery orders. Separate physical tablet for Uber Eats.
painPoints: Duplicates DoorDash tablet problem — two separate systems
Menu 86 updates require manual entry on both platforms
Payout reconciliation is manual and time-consuming

toolStack.name: Instagram & TikTok
toolStack.usage: Posts 2-3 times/week. Creates content on her phone. No scheduling tool. No analytics tracking.
painPoints: Inconsistent posting — some weeks 5 posts, some weeks 0
No content calendar or strategy
No connection between social media performance and actual revenue
Catering is barely promoted despite being high-margin

toolStack.name: Google Sheets
toolStack.usage: Staff schedule built manually every Sunday night. Texts screenshot to team. Shift swaps via group text.
painPoints: Priya spends 3-4 hours every Sunday on scheduling
No visibility into labor cost vs. revenue by shift
Shift swaps are chaotic — no formal approval process
No-shows happen weekly with no backup system

toolStack.name: Paper Notebook
toolStack.usage: All catering orders tracked in a physical notebook. No calendar integration or digital backup.
painPoints: Single point of failure — if notebook is lost, all catering data is gone
No calendar integration for venue or capacity planning
No automated reminders or client follow-ups
Nadia is part-time — gaps in coverage when she's not in

toolStack.name: QuickBooks Online
toolStack.usage: Basic bookkeeping by contractor who comes in biweekly. Always 2-3 weeks behind.
painPoints: Priya doesn't have a clear picture of cash flow at any given moment
Always 2-3 weeks behind — financial data is stale
No automated categorization of transactions
Food cost analysis requires manual calculation

toolStack.name: Yelp & Google Business
toolStack.usage: Responds to some reviews when Priya remembers to check. No system for generating positive reviews.
painPoints: 4.3 stars on Google vs. 4.6 and 4.5 for two competitors within 3 blocks
Negative reviews about wait times go unanswered for days
No system for soliciting positive reviews from happy customers

workflows.name: Inventory & Food Ordering
workflows.description: The process of tracking ingredient levels and placing orders with food suppliers to keep the kitchen stocked.
workflows.currentProcess: Ethan walks the walk-in cooler and dry storage → mentally notes what's low → calls or texts suppliers to place orders → deliveries arrive at various times → no systematic tracking of what was ordered vs. received vs. used.
painPoints: Runs out of key ingredients 2-3 times per month, resulting in 86'd menu items
Food waste estimated at 12-15% (industry target is 4-8%)
Over-orders on some items, under-orders on others
No connection between POS sales data and ordering decisions
All ordering knowledge lives in Ethan's head — single point of failure
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could analyze POS sales data to predict ingredient needs, automatically generate purchase orders, and alert Ethan when items approach reorder points — reducing waste and 86'd items dramatically.

workflows.name: Staff Scheduling
workflows.description: Weekly process of building and communicating the staff schedule and managing last-minute changes.
workflows.currentProcess: Priya builds next week's schedule on Sunday night in Google Sheets → texts a screenshot to the group chat → staff request changes via text → Priya manually updates the sheet → texts the updated version.
painPoints: Priya spends 3-4 hours every Sunday building the schedule
No visibility into labor cost vs. revenue by shift
Shift swaps are chaotic — handled entirely through group text
No-shows happen weekly, costing overtime for emergency coverage
No forecasting of staffing needs based on historical data
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could analyze historical revenue by day/time to recommend staffing levels, auto-generate a draft schedule, and manage shift swap requests through a simple approval workflow.

workflows.name: Social Media & Marketing
workflows.description: Creating, scheduling, and publishing social media content to drive foot traffic, delivery orders, and catering inquiries.
workflows.currentProcess: Priya takes photos on her phone during prep or service → writes captions herself → posts directly to Instagram and TikTok when she has time → no scheduling, no content calendar, no analytics tracking.
painPoints: Inconsistent posting — some weeks 5 posts, some weeks 0
No content calendar or strategy — purely reactive
No tracking of which posts drive traffic or orders
Catering is barely marketed despite being a high-margin revenue stream
Priya is the only person who posts — single point of failure
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could generate a content calendar, draft captions based on daily specials and events, suggest optimal posting times based on engagement data, and create catering-specific campaigns.

workflows.name: Online Reviews & Reputation
workflows.description: Monitoring reviews across Google, Yelp, and DoorDash and responding to maintain the restaurant's reputation.
workflows.currentProcess: Priya checks Google and Yelp when she remembers. Responds to negative reviews (usually days later). No system for soliciting positive reviews from happy customers.
painPoints: 4.3 stars on Google while two nearby competitors have 4.5-4.6
Negative reviews about wait times go unanswered for days
No proactive review solicitation from happy customers
DoorDash reviews are rarely monitored
No tracking of review volume trends
workflows.aiOpportunity: AI could monitor all review platforms, draft personalized responses (empathetic for negative, grateful for positive), route for Priya's approval, and trigger post-visit review requests via receipt or SMS.

eventTypes.name: Catering Inquiry

cateringInquiries: We're planning a company lunch for about 40 people at our office on Monroe Ave. Looking for a grain bowl spread with a few protein options. We try to do this quarterly.
I'm getting married in September and we want Rapids Bite to cater our rehearsal dinner. Around 55 guests, outdoor venue in Ada. We love your Mediterranean flavors.
Can you do a corporate lunch for 25 people? We have a team meeting on the 14th. Would need it delivered to the Amway Grand area by noon.
Our office has about 18 people and we want to try a catering lunch on a Tuesday. Budget is around $14-16 per person. Half of us are vegetarian.
I'm planning a graduation party for my daughter — 60-70 guests, backyard in East Grand Rapids. Would love a wrap and bowl station setup.
We're a nonprofit on Cherry St and we have a donor reception coming up. Maybe 35 guests, evening. We want something elevated but not stuffy.
I'm looking for catering for a 30-person baby shower. Daytime, private event space in Heritage Hill. Several guests are vegan or gluten-free.
Our law firm (12 people) wants a working lunch catered once a week for the next month as a trial. Wraps and salads ideally. Downtown location.
Can you cater a birthday dinner party? It's my husband's 50th, 45 people, we're using a venue on Fulton St. He loves Korean and Middle Eastern food.
I manage a co-working space near Wealthy St and I'm interested in setting up a weekly catering account. 20-30 people on average.
We need boxed lunches for a training day — 50 people, mix of dietary needs. Need them by 11:30am, we're in Wyoming, MI. Is that too far for delivery?
Planning a bridal shower, about 20 guests. We love your brand and want a lighter, fresh food experience. Midtown venue.
I'm the event coordinator at a tech company in Walker. We have 80 people for a product launch event. Need passed bites and a grain bowl station, evening.
Hi, I'm organizing a community fundraiser at Garfield Park — about 120 people. We need affordable catering options around $12-14 per person.
I'd like to inquire about catering for our company holiday party. About 55 people, downtown GR hotel ballroom. December date TBD.
I'm a caterer myself but I want to sub out the food for a small corporate gig — 30 people, want grain bowls and wraps only, budget about $500 total. Is that feasible?
Our hospital department (30 people) is doing a staff appreciation lunch. We have strict nut allergy concerns — is your kitchen nut-free?
I saw you at the ArtPrize vendor setup last year and I've been meaning to reach out. We want a food drop for a private art opening, 40 guests, Fulton Heights gallery.
We're doing a retirement party for a longtime teacher — about 65 guests, evening event, community center in Creston neighborhood.
I manage HR for a 200-person company on the East Beltline. We want to do a quarterly catering rotation and you came highly recommended. Let's talk volume pricing.
Planning a gender reveal party — 35 guests, backyard in Alger Heights. We'd love wraps, bowls, and maybe your watermelon juice? Very casual vibe.
We're a real estate team, 12 people, and we close on a big project next month. Want to do a catered celebration lunch. Probably Eastown or East Hills for delivery.
I'm the principal at a local middle school. We want to reward our staff — 45 people — with a catered lunch on an early release day. Healthy food is important to us.
Is there a minimum order for catering? I just need food for 15 people for a team lunch. We work in a small office on Lake Dr SE.
I'm having a Diwali celebration for friends and family — about 50 guests. I love that your food has global flavors. Any chance you could do an Indian-inspired spread?
Our startup is hosting an investor demo day downtown. 25 attendees. We want food to feel fresh and high-quality — makes us look good too.
I need catering for a wake reception after a memorial service. About 80 guests, Celebration of Life format. Something warm and comforting. Diverse family with varied dietary needs.
We run a fitness studio and want to offer a healthy post-class lunch once a month for our community — about 30 people. Would love grain bowls.
Planning a team-building offsite for a 22-person company. We're renting a venue in the country. Need full catering: lunch and afternoon snacks.
I need boxed lunches for a morning training from 8-noon — 35 people. We'd like them delivered by 7:45am if possible. Is that in your service window?

eventTypes.automationDescription: AI drafts a personalized catering proposal with menu suggestions based on guest count and budget, calculates pricing, and sends to Nadia for review before responding to the inquiry.

eventTypes.name: New Online Review

reviewTexts: The Korean BBQ Bowl is absolutely incredible. I've been here four times in three weeks. Enough said.
Best fast-casual spot in GR by a mile. The ingredients are fresh, the portions are generous, and the staff actually cares about what they're making.
I discovered this place through DoorDash and immediately had to come in person. Everything from scratch, I can tell.
The Tropical Green Juice alone is worth the trip. Had it three days in a row last week.
Finally, a healthy restaurant that doesn't taste healthy. I mean that as the highest compliment.
My whole office orders from here every Friday. We've tried everything on the menu. No miss yet.
Five stars for the falafel wrap alone. I dream about that tahini.
Solid grain bowls, super customizable. I can eat here every day without getting bored. Genuinely my favorite place to eat in Grand Rapids.
I have celiac disease and this is one of the few places where I actually trust the gluten-free option. The staff takes it seriously.
Came in on my lunch break on a busy Thursday. Was in and out in 11 minutes with a full meal. That's impressive.
The Moroccan Spiced Bowl hit every flavor note. Warm, earthy, bright. Clearly made by people who know food.
Priya was behind the counter when I came in and she remembered my usual order from three visits ago. That kind of thing keeps me coming back.
I've tried most healthy fast-casual places in GR. This is the best. Not close.
The harissa chicken wrap is unreal. Ordered it on a whim and now I can't stop thinking about it.
My kids even love it here — and they hate anything green. Getting them to eat a spinach bowl is a miracle. Thank you.
I ordered delivery and somehow the bowl was still fresh and beautiful when it arrived. Clearly packaged with care.
The miso ginger bowl is one of the best things I've eaten in Grand Rapids period. Not just fast-casual — period.
Staff is always friendly and they move fast even when the line is long. Good energy in this place.
One of my favorite things about this place is that I never feel gross after eating here. It's satisfying but light. Love it.
This spot filled a gap in GR that I didn't even know existed. Global flavors, real ingredients, fast service. What else do you want?
Gave two stars because the avocado I got was still underripe and mushy. This has happened twice. Please check your produce before putting it on bowls.
The wait on Saturday afternoon was 20 minutes for a grain bowl. I get that it's popular but I almost left. Speed needs to improve on weekends.
My DoorDash order was missing a full protein — I ordered chicken, got no chicken. Had to eat a rice and veggie bowl for $15. Not ideal.
Three stars. Food is great but the portions have gotten noticeably smaller over the past few months. I used to be full. Now I'm not.
Ordered via Uber Eats and the dressing was missing. It was a dressing-heavy bowl. Without it the whole thing was dry. Disappointing for the price.
I've had two bad experiences with undercooked rice. The flavor of everything else is great but please check the rice before it goes out.
Two stars. Came in 45 minutes before close and was told half the menu was already 86'd. If you close at 8, please be stocked until 8.
The line was out the door on a Tuesday at noon. That tells you everything you need to know. Worth the wait but you'll wait.
I don't understand the hype. It was fine. Grain bowls are grain bowls. Nothing I couldn't make at home.
Great food but the music is always too loud for what is essentially a chill healthy lunch spot. Dialing it back by 30% would improve the vibe.
I've been vegetarian for 10 years and finding a fast-casual spot this good is genuinely exciting. The tofu options are phenomenal.
The Cali Avocado Wrap is clean, fresh, and perfectly assembled. It's my go-to every time I need a quick lunch that doesn't feel like a compromise.
I ordered catering for my office and it was flawless. Setup was easy, food stayed fresh, everyone raved. Will absolutely use them again.
This place has ruined other fast-casual for me. Everything else just feels like a downgrade now.
The Korean BBQ Bowl is back on the menu and my whole week just got better. Please never 86 it again.
Quick, healthy, affordable, local. Four things that rarely go together. This place nails all four.
I'm a picky eater and I can build a bowl here that I actually love. The customization is a big deal for me.
One of my employees told me about this place and I drove across town to try it. Now I bring my whole team here for lunch.
Ordered the ahi tuna bowl — listed on the menu but they were out. Wish they'd update the digital menu when things run out. Wasted order.
I asked if the peanut sauce had peanuts (I have a mild allergy) and the counter person went back and checked the actual ingredients for me. That's the right response.
The smoothie options are underrated. The turmeric ginger blend was just what I needed after a workout.
Had a birthday celebration here with 8 friends. Staff was super accommodating, moved tables for us. Great community energy.
I've ordered delivery four times from DoorDash. Three times were perfect. Once was a disaster — missing items, arrived cold. Inconsistent but mostly great.
A little pricey for a quick lunch at $16-17 once you add a juice, but the quality justifies it. I just have to remind myself of that each time.
I love this place but wish they had more parking. Circling the Wealthy Street block three times to find a spot is a deterrent for weekday lunch.
I drove past this place for a year before trying it. Once I did I immediately regretted waiting so long. Get in here.
The falafel is clearly made in-house and it shows. Crispy outside, fluffy inside. Way better than anywhere else I've had it in GR.
As someone who works remotely and eats lunch out often, I've found my spot. Laptop-friendly, consistent wifi, great food.
Their catering fed my whole team and the feedback was unanimous — people wanted to know where it came from immediately.
I'm from Chicago and I'll say this: the grain bowl scene here punches above its weight. Genuinely impressed.

eventTypes.automationDescription: AI analyzes sentiment, identifies specific complaints (wait time, item quality, service), drafts a personalized response, routes to Priya for one-click approval, and logs the interaction.

eventTypes.name: Staff Schedule Change Request
eventTypes.automationDescription: AI checks the current schedule for coverage gaps, identifies available staff who can cover, drafts a replacement request message, and notifies Priya with a recommended resolution.

eventTypes.name: Daily Sales Summary
eventTypes.automationDescription: AI generates a concise daily digest for Priya and Ethan: revenue vs. target, food cost flag if over 32%, top/bottom performers, and one inventory reorder recommendation based on what sold.

metadata.notes: Built-in reference template. Represents a typical 15-25 person fast-casual or independent restaurant. High demo value for hospitality, retail, and any customer-facing business with thin margins.
